solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Bitterness of those downtrodden in the wine industry? (4,6)

blocks.note: the straight reading: resentment, especially disparaging what you failed to get

blocks.clueFragment: those downtrodden in the wine industry?
blocks.note: the playful reading: fruit trodden underfoot at the winery, and tasting sharp

annotation.surface: A glum thought about the grapes crushed underfoot at a winery.
annotation.walkthrough: Sour grapes is resentful bitterness, from the fox who calls the grapes he cannot reach sour. The question mark flags the whimsical second reading about treading grapes.
annotation.definitionFit: Sour grapes is the bitterness of pretending not to want what you cannot have.

entries.clue: Languages bores actor in play (5-5)

definitions.note: Serbo-Croat is one name covering the closely related Serbian and Croatian, hence the plural

indicators.note: letters in play are moving about, free to be rearranged

annotation.surface: A tedious performer drones on during a stage production.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Languages' reads as the subject of 'bores', but it is the definition; 'in play' sounds theatrical next to 'actor' and is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Serbo-Croat is the name for the South Slavic languages spoken in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Montenegro.

entries.clue: Vase or bag, reportedly? (3)

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to bag money is to earn it

annotation.walkthrough: 'Vase or bag' looks like two containers side by side; 'bag' is a verb here, meaning to get or earn.
annotation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase, typically one with a foot and a rounded body.

entries.clue: Filling for vegan? A cherry and chocolate sauce (7)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, as a filling

annotation.surface: A menu question about what to put in a vegan dessert: cherry plus chocolate sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Filling' is at home on a dessert menu, which disguises its job of pointing inside the next words.
annotation.definitionFit: Ganache is a smooth sauce or filling of chocolate melted with cream.

entries.clue: Learner in a musical lit up (6)

indicators.note: the learner goes in, inside the other letters

blocks.note: Fame, the stage and screen musical

annotation.surface: A novice performer starring in a show.
annotation.walkthrough: L goes inside A FAME, splitting FAME after its F.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something aflame is burning, lit up in the sense of set alight.

entries.clue: Poems translated in classics course (5)

indicators.note: to translate is to change the form, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Verse rendered into English as part of a Latin and Greek degree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Classics course' reads as a university subject; it means a racecourse. Epsom Downs, in Surrey, hosts the Derby and the Oaks, two of the five British flat-racing classics.
annotation.definitionFit: Epsom is the racecourse where two of the classic races are run.

entries.clue: Gate’s opening into latrine after turning key (8)

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter
the letters turn about into a new order

blocks.note: G goes into it before the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone unlocks a gate and it swings into an outdoor toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like the thing that is turned in a lock, but it is the definition, used as an adjective meaning essential.
annotation.definitionFit: Something integral is essential, key to the whole.

entries.clue: Leader of negotiations brought into bankruptcy dispute (3-2)

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the letter is brought inside the next word

annotation.surface: A company's chief negotiator gets dragged into an insolvency row.
annotation.walkthrough: N goes into RUIN between U and I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for an argument or brush with someone, as in a run-in with the police.

entries.clue: Unsuccessful crime written into journal (6)

indicators.note: the crime is written inside the journal

blocks.note: a log is a journal, as a ship's log
a sin is a wrong, a crime

annotation.surface: A failed offence recorded in someone's diary.
annotation.walkthrough: SIN is the crossword's usual stand-in for a wrongdoing, and LOG for any record kept day by day.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in adjectival use: the losing team is the unsuccessful one.

entries.clue: Odd right, as even number even! (10)

indicators.note: odd letters are strange, put into an unusual order

annotation.surface: A puzzled cry that something odd could be even, as though numbers could switch sides.
annotation.walkthrough: Odd and even look like a maths joke; 'Odd' rearranges RIGHT AS, and the last 'even' is a verb meaning make level.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to straighten a line or edge is to even it, making it level.

entries.clue: Electrical unit in farmhouse switched over (3)

indicators.note: the letters are in the next word
turned the other way round, so read backwards

annotation.surface: Someone flips a light switch in a farmhouse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Switched' suits an electrical scene, but here it turns the hidden MHO round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain equivalence: the ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance, named after Georg Ohm.

entries.clue: Lie about gallery’s support for young woman (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other

blocks.note: a miss is a young woman
the Tate, the London art gallery

annotation.surface: Someone fibs about a gallery's sponsorship of a young artist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lie about' seems to be followed by what the lie concerns; it is the definition. The Tate is a group of British art galleries, the best known in London.
annotation.definitionFit: To misstate something is to report it falsely, to lie about it.

entries.clue: French produce associate put in kitty (9)

indicators.note: the associate is put inside the kitty

blocks.note: an associate is a member of a club or body

annotation.surface: A French farmer's colleague chips money into a shared pot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a shared fund of money, but it is a cat.
annotation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft cheese made in Normandy, a French product.

entries.clue: Slice of meat — more unwise? (6)

blocks.note: a thin cut of bacon, as served at breakfast
the comparative of an adjective meaning hasty or reckless

annotation.walkthrough: The dash joins two readings into one scene: RASHER the slice of bacon, and RASHER the comparative of rash.
annotation.surface: Wondering whether another slice of bacon would be a poor choice.
annotation.definitionFit: A rasher is a thin slice of bacon; rasher is also the comparative of rash.

entries.clue: Translation of phrase for skilled mountain climber (6)

indicators.note: translating changes a text's form, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A phrasebook entry for talking to an expert climber.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Translation' sits naturally beside 'phrase', which hides that it asks for the letters of PHRASE to be reordered.
annotation.definitionFit: The Sherpa people of Nepal are famed as skilled Himalayan climbers and guides.

entries.clue: Journalist observed what could lead to cuts (7)

blocks.note: a hack is a journalist, usually a low-grade one

annotation.surface: A reporter spotted something that might bring about spending cuts.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a news story about budget cuts; the cuts are literal ones made by a saw.
annotation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a tool used to cut metal.

entries.clue: Capital city hasn’t changed with invasion of English (6)

indicators.note: the letters are changed round
the E invades, going inside the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: A capital that has stayed the same despite an English invasion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hasn't changed' reads as a statement that nothing moved; 'changed' is the instruction to rearrange HASNT.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Athens is one capital city, that of Greece.

entries.clue: Polar region that’s intact shaped around curved line (9)

indicators.note: the letters are shaped into a new form
the rearranged letters go around the curve

blocks.note: an arc is a curved line

annotation.surface: A polar landscape left unspoilt, shaped around a curving line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Intact' suggests untouched wilderness, which suits the scene, but it is the letters to be shaped.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain equivalence: the Antarctic names the region round the South Pole.

entries.clue: Huge animal Greek character chains up at home (5)

indicators.note: to chain someone up is to confine them, so RHO holds IN

annotation.surface: A large beast, a Greek man and chains, at home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person in the story, and it is a letter of the alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the rhinoceros, shortened to rhino, is one huge animal, weighing up to two tonnes.

entries.clue: Part of the body — lap? (3)

blocks.note: a single stage of a race or journey

annotation.walkthrough: 'Lap' next to 'body' suggests the part you sit a child on; it means a stage of a race.
annotation.definitionFit: A leg is a limb, and also one stage, or lap, of a journey or race.

entries.clue: Industrial action hit (6)

blocks.note: a verb meaning to deliver a blow

annotation.walkthrough: Two readings of one word: STRIKE as a walkout by workers, and STRIKE as a verb meaning to hit.
annotation.surface: Industrial action has landed a blow.
annotation.definitionFit: A strike is a stoppage of work; to strike is also to hit.

entries.clue: Sense location through hearing (5)

indicators.note: the word is got through the ear, by its sound

annotation.surface: Working out where a sound comes from by listening.
annotation.walkthrough: Hearing is itself a sense, which tempts the solver towards it; the answer is a different sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: sight is one of the five senses, alongside hearing.

entries.clue: Some sparkling emerald — is it? (3)

indicators.note: some of the letters, a run inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: Holding up a glittering green stone and asking whether it is real.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a sparkling emerald is indeed a gem.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: the whole clue reads straight, since an emerald that sparkles is a precious stone.

entries.clue: Rider saw moorhen flying about (10)

indicators.note: letters flying about land in a new order

annotation.surface: A rider out on horseback spots a waterbird flapping around.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flying' fits the bird perfectly, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A horsewoman is a woman who rides horses.
